candidates.exact_span: Water quality-based requirements are necessary where effluent limits more stringent than technology-based limits are necessary to maintain or achieve federal or state water quality limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the condition under which water quality-based effluent limits supplement or replace technology-based limits; a different reading of when WQBELs are 'necessary' changes which numeric limits are treated as applicable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent limitations and/or conditions established in the draft permit are in compliance with applicable State WQS and applicable State water quality management plans to assure that surface WQS of the receiving waters are protected and maintained, or attained.
candidates.computation_change_reason: References a 'draft permit' and ties operative limits to State WQS compliance; interpretation of whether draft-permit limits are the enforceable FY2025 limits, and which WQS version grounds them, affects which numeric limits are selected for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The facility discharge point into the San Juan River is in State of New Mexico waters approximately two miles upstream of the Navajo Nation's boundary.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Locates the discharge relative to state and tribal jurisdictional boundaries; different readings of whether limits are evaluated at the point of discharge only or must also protect downstream tribal waters change which standard set and segment criteria govern applicable limits and how missing or ambiguous evidence for downstream-protective parameters is classified.

candidates.exact_span: Since 40 CFR §122.4(d) requires NPDES permits also be protective of a downstream state or tribe's water quality standards, the water quality standards of the Navajo Nation have been considered.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Invokes downstream-protection authority and states tribal standards were 'considered' rather than specifying how they translate into permit limits or conditions; interpretation of whether this creates separate enforceable limits or monitoring/condition obligations beyond New Mexico point-of-discharge standards changes applicable limit selection and whether additional requirements were in force.

candidates.exact_span: Where these technology-based permit limits do not protect water quality or the designated uses, additional water quality-based effluent limitations and/or conditions are included in the NPDES permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines when supplemental WQBELs and permit conditions are added; different readings of whether a given parameter's technology-based limit 'protects' designated uses determine whether a WQBEL or associated condition (potentially including monitoring) is operative for that parameter.

candidates.exact_span: State narrative and numerical water quality standards are used in conjunction with EPA criteria and other available toxicity information to determine the adequacy of technology-based permit limits and the need for additional water quality-based controls.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the inputs and method for deciding whether technology-based limits suffice or additional numeric WQBELs are required; interpretation of which narrative standards, EPA criteria, or toxicity data are operative changes the derived applicable numeric limit for a parameter.

candidates.exact_span: The general and specific stream standards are provided in New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Water (20.6.4 NMAC, effective September 12, 2018).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the governing New Mexico regulatory standard compilation and its effective date; a different reading of which NMAC version or effective date applies during Federal FY2025 changes which numerical criteria are used to establish applicable discharge limits.

candidates.exact_span: The facility discharges into the San Juan River in segment number 20.6.4.401 of the San Juan Basin.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigns the receiving water to a specific New Mexico basin segment; interpretation of segment 20.6.4.401 versus an alternative segment classification changes which segment-specific numerical standards apply to the discharge.

candidates.exact_span: The designated uses of the receiving waters are public and industrial water supply, irrigation, livestock watering, wildlife habitat, primary contact, marginal coldwater aquatic life and warmwater aquatic life.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Lists New Mexico designated uses that drive water quality criteria selection; different interpretation of which uses are actually designated at the discharge point (e.g., marginal coldwater versus warmwater aquatic life) changes the numeric criteria from which applicable WQBELs are derived.

candidates.exact_span: The general and specific stream standards for the Navajo Nation (NN) are provided in Surface Water Quality Standards (NNWQS) passed by Navajo Nation Resources Committee on May 13, 2008, effective March 26, 2009.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies the authoritative Navajo Nation standard set and its effective date for parameters where tribal standards may govern; interpretation of whether and when NNWQS rather than NMAC criteria apply changes the numeric limit used for those parameters.

candidates.exact_span: The Navajo Nation WQS and New Mexico WQS are very similar and protection to NMWQS at the point of discharge would also be protective of downstream Navajo Nation waters, except for some of the parameters as discussed below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States that New Mexico limits at the point of discharge are generally sufficient for downstream tribal protection but carves out unspecified parameters; interpretation of which parameters fall in the exception (referenced but not defined in this segment) changes whether NM or NN-derived limits apply and whether missing or incomplete evidence for those parameters should be treated as unresolved rather than covered by NM standards.

candidates.exact_span: The Navajo Nation designated uses of the San Juan River at the point it enters the Navajo Nation are domestic water supply, primary human contact, secondary human contact, agricultural water supply, fish consumption, aquatic & wildlife habitat and livestock watering.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Lists downstream tribal designated uses that may differ from New Mexico uses at the point of discharge; for parameters in the NN-exception category, interpretation of which tribal use drives the controlling criterion changes the applicable numeric limit derived for downstream protection.
